question: Half of the length of the chord of a circle is 12 cm and the perpendicular distance between the centre and the chord is 5 cm. The radius of the circle is:
solution:
Given:

The length of the chord of a circle is 24 cm, and the perpendicular distance between the centre and the chord is 5 cm. 

Concept used:

Chord Length Using Perpendicular Distance from the Center = 2 × √(R² - d²)

(Where r = radius of the circle, d = distance between the centre and the chord)

Calculation:

Let the radius of the circle be R.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51edf17397128cd7ef274df6bff311c338126aec11e03ede7828866bd4d502b0.png] 

Here,

AB = 24 cm long chord

OD = Perpendicular distance between the centre and chord

OB = Radius

​According to the concept,

24 = 2 × √(R2 - d2)" id="MathJax-Element-16-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">√" id="MathJax-Element-19-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">√" id="MathJax-Element-37-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">√ 

⇒ 12 = √(R2 - d2)" id="MathJax-Element-17-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">√" id="MathJax-Element-20-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">√" id="MathJax-Element-38-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">√ 

⇒ 144 = R² - 5²

⇒ R² = 169

⇒ R = 13

∴ The radius of the circle is 13 cm.
